content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

This is a securitisation Transfer and Servicing Agreement rather than a procurement contract, so the IP rule maps onto ownership of the Receivables, Receivable Files and servicing records. On those material terms the document already sits at or above the preferred position for us:

- **We own the assets outright.** The Depositor "transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer... all of the Depositor's right, title and interest" in the Receivables and related Transferred Property (p0033, p0035).
- **Our files are held for our benefit, not the Vendor's.** Cellco holds the Receivable Files as Custodian "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee" (p0138), constructively delivered to the Indenture Trustee as pledgee (p0142), and must deliver them to the Indenture Trustee or a successor custodian on termination at its own expense (p0147), and to a Successor Servicer along with its servicing records (p0346).
- **Nothing of ours flows to the counterparty.** No assignment or licence of our IP or data to Cellco, and no joint ownership — so the walk-away triggers are absent. The one retention clause (p0346) covers only Cellco's own processes, models and servicing software, which is the expressly permitted Vendor-platform/generic-tools carve-out.

Two points short of the ideal that I recorded in the rationale rather than flagging, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements:

1. Access to and return of our own Receivable Files is "subject to" Cellco's unilaterally-set legal, regulatory, privacy and data protection policies (p0146, p0147, p0338), with a catch-all in p0346. This qualifies the delivery mechanics but cannot defeat our ownership — and it is properly a records/audit-access point, so flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term.
2. There is no express licence-back to Cellco's servicing systems to smooth a servicing transition.
